directAnswer: An electric vehicle (EV) that is cheaper than a petrol car can last anywhere from 8 to 15 years, depending on usage, maintenance, and battery technology.
summary: The lifespan of an EV is influenced by various factors including battery health, driving habits, and maintenance practices.

sections.heading: Battery Life and Longevity
sections.body: The battery is a crucial component of an EV, typically lasting between 8 to 15 years. Regular charging habits and temperature conditions can impact battery performance.

sections.heading: Factors Affecting Lifespan
sections.body: Factors such as driving conditions, frequency of charging, and regular maintenance can significantly influence how long an EV lasts compared to a petrol car.

sections.heading: Cost Comparison Over Time
sections.body: While the initial purchase price of an EV may be lower, the total cost of ownership, including maintenance and energy costs, should be analyzed over the vehicle's lifespan.

steps.title: Evaluate Battery Health
steps.detail: Check the battery health regularly using the vehicle's onboard diagnostics or a third-party app to ensure longevity.

steps.title: Adopt Efficient Charging Practices
steps.detail: Charge your EV during off-peak hours and avoid frequent fast charging to prolong battery life.

steps.title: Schedule Regular Maintenance
steps.detail: Follow the manufacturer's recommended maintenance schedule to keep the EV in optimal condition.

faqs.question: What is the average lifespan of an EV battery?
faqs.answer: The average lifespan of an EV battery is typically between 8 to 15 years, depending on usage and care.

faqs.question: How does an EV's lifespan compare to that of a petrol car?
faqs.answer: EVs generally have a similar or longer lifespan than petrol cars, primarily due to fewer moving parts and less mechanical wear.

faqs.question: Can I extend the life of my EV?
faqs.answer: Yes, by following good charging practices, maintaining the vehicle, and avoiding extreme temperatures, you can extend the life of your EV.

caveats: Battery technology is rapidly evolving, and future advancements may change lifespan expectations.
Actual lifespan can vary based on individual usage patterns and environmental factors.
